Sarg.et: From Middle High German sarc, from Old High German sark, sarh, from Proto-West Germanic *sark (“grave, coffin”), ultimately from Greek sarcophagus. Cognate with Hunsrik Saarich, Sarrich.

s: a female given name from Biblical Hebrew; variant form Sarah

Sarkophag.et: Borrowed from French sarcophage, from Latin sarcophagus, from Ancient Greek σαρκοφάγος (sarkophágos, “coffin of limestone”, noun), from σαρκοφάγος (sarkophágos, “flesh-eating, carnivorous”), from σάρξ (sárx, “flesh, meat”) + -φάγος (-phágos).
